static_findings.snippet: Stop writing `if (x !== null && x !== undefined)` everywhere.
- `O.flatMap(fn)` = "if we have something, apply this function"
- `O.getOrElse(() => default)` = "unwrap, or use this default if nothing"
**Plain language:** `flatMap` means "if this succeeded, try the next thing"
| Default for missing | "Use this if nothing" | `O.getOrElse(() => default)` |
| Transform if present | "If something, change it" | `O.map(fn)` |
| Chain nullable operations | "If something, try this" | `O.flatMap(fn)` |
| Wrap throwing function | "Try this, catch errors" | `E.tryCatch(fn, onError)` |
| Handle both cases | "Do this for error, that for success" | `E.fold(onLeft, onRight)` |

content.value_statement: fp-ts can feel abstract when teams need practical TypeScript patterns for nullable values, errors, and async work. This skill shows when to use pipe, Option, Either, map, flatMap, and when to keep code simple.
actual_capabilities: Explains when pipe improves TypeScript transformation chains.
Shows how Option replaces repeated null and undefined checks.
Demonstrates Either for expected validation and parsing failures.
Compares simple imperative code with fp-ts alternatives.
Provides refactoring examples for callbacks, validation, and Promise flows.
Gives a concise cheat sheet for common fp-ts functions.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not an automated refactoring tool.
It does not validate project-specific fp-ts versions or compiler settings.
It focuses on common patterns, not advanced category theory concepts.
It does not replace tests for refactored TypeScript behavior.

use_cases.title: Introduce fp-ts Safely
use_cases.description: Guide a TypeScript team through practical pipe, Option, and Either patterns without overwhelming new users.

use_cases.title: Refactor Error Handling
use_cases.description: Convert expected parsing or validation failures into explicit Either results with readable control flow.

use_cases.title: Review Functional Code
use_cases.description: Decide whether an fp-ts abstraction improves readability or should remain simple TypeScript.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner guidance for a small TypeScript function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript function and tell me whether pipe, Option, Either, or plain TypeScript is the clearest choice. Explain the tradeoff briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Nullable Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace repeated null checks with a readable option flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this nullable TypeScript access pattern using fp-ts Option only if it improves readability. Keep the result simple and explain why.

prompt_templates.title: Make Errors Explicit
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert expected exceptions into typed return values.
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this parsing or validation logic with fp-ts Either. Use clear error values and show how the caller should handle both outcomes.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Async Composition
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for multi-step async work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this async TypeScript workflow for TaskEither. Refactor only the parts that benefit from explicit failure handling and preserve readability.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether to wrap a two-step lookup in Option.
output_examples.output: The response recommends optional chaining for the simple case, then explains when Option becomes useful for longer chains.

output_examples.input: A validation function throws errors for expected user input failures.
output_examples.output: The response proposes explicit Either results with human-readable error cases and a clear caller handling path.

output_examples.input: A reviewer sees a dense fp-ts pipeline in production code.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the readability risk and suggests simpler intermediate variables or a shorter pipeline.

best_practices: Use fp-ts when it makes failure, absence, or transformation flow clearer.
Prefer simple TypeScript when optional chaining or loops are easier to read.
Introduce one pattern at a time and keep examples close to real code.
anti_patterns: Do not use fp-ts to impress readers when direct TypeScript is clearer.
Do not hide business rules inside dense pipelines that reviewers cannot scan.
Do not refactor behavior without tests that cover success and failure paths.

faq.question: Does this skill require category theory knowledge?
faq.answer: No. It explains fp-ts through plain TypeScript examples and practical tradeoffs.

faq.question: Can it refactor my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides an AI assistant or developer, but changes still need review and testing.

faq.question: Which fp-ts patterns does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers pipe, Option, Either, map, flatMap, TaskEither basics, and common readability checks.

faq.question: Is this useful for teams new to functional programming?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes incremental adoption and warns against patterns that reduce readability.

faq.question: Does it replace TypeScript language features?
faq.answer: No. It often recommends optional chaining, loops, or direct code when they are clearer.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
